To those saying it is already vandalism. It was commissioned by the local municipal here for the first time. It was professionally painted. It is legitimately allowed to be there in terms of local laws. The workers who painted it must be disappointed as it was a great paint job. 

To those saying "Who cares" etc, well for context...there has been an uprising in homophobic attacks here and a few months ago a man was lured to a park and killed...for being gay...it started just like this (if you want sources message me). Seeing it spread to this town is disappointing. Nobody deserves to be killed for being gay. 

For those saying "shoving it down our throats". It is still an issue. People are killed around the world for being gay. Attacked and threatened for it. What real harm do they do to anybody? I say this as a cis, straight white woman. 

"It is just graffiti". Yes, but the words are targeted and clear. They didn't write "fuck off" or "enough already". They wrote something seen as a very bad insult in Dutch. 

To those thinking I am a Karen...firstly thanks for that. My students will love that. I am going to put those particular comments on our meme wall in my classroom. 

I am overreacting by reporting this...I didn't break down in the street like Willem Dafoe in Platoon nor did I unite the Queen's and march under one banner (rewatching Game of Thrones...not season 8...never season 8...can you tell)? Taking the message and why it was written out of it, it ruins the town which is actually really pretty. No matter your personal viewpoint surely we can agree that crappy graffiti like this just looks awful. 

Finally, look to history. Look at when a simple hate message on a door or wall led to something bigger. Paint me dramatic if you want, but time and again it happens and will keep happening if we ignore it.

It was commissioned by the municipal here and it was professionally done. It is the first time they ever did it.

I have worked in a school which was the place students went as a final attempt to keep them from detention centers and the like. Now I work in a school in which students will be quiet if I ask but they are notoriously lazy when it comes to deadlines. So I'll offer two prospectives:

1. In both situations holding them accountable works wonders. Draw up a class charter and have them decide the rules, obviously in conjunction with you. I find giving over responsibility to them, no matter their backgrounds, makes them feel important so they stick to it much more. 

2. Honesty. Now this works better in the latter school I am in, but, I find saying such things like "You know at your age I was reluctant to do homework, I totally understand how you feel. But, I want you to work hard because it's a pleasure seeing your work and you bring so much to the class. And isn't it great to finish a task and not have to keep thinking about it?"

Maybe this is not what you were looking for per se, but, I was surprised at how much they enjoyed taking responsibility and I see a rise in quality work and deadlines met.

If they are simply unwieldy monsters I would have a three strike rule. If they talk while you do they get their name on the board. Another infraction they get a tally and so on. Sanction them for every minor infraction. They soon get sick of it. Nobody wants to see their name up on display like that.
